http://www.euronews.com/2026/09/06/fligh.text: Indonesia's Soekarno–Hatta International Airport suspended flight operations on Sunday after an eruption of the Anak Krakatoa volcano.Mount Anak Krakatoa began erupting on Saturday, producing a lava fountain and "booming sounds and tremors" that were reported by residents in several parts of the country, according to Indonesia's geology agency.Authorities suspended operations at the airport from 1:30 am local time on Sunday morning after ash from the volcano was detected in the airspace surrounding the airport."The latest paper test…showed positive results indicating the spread of volcanic ash in the Soekarno-Hatta International Airport area, consequently the airport closure was extended until Sunday at 09:30 am (0230 GMT)," Indonesia's transport ministry said in a statement.More than 22,000 passengers have been affected by the suspension, the ministry said, with 209 flights impacted, in particular to and from Singapore.Routes to destinations including Doha, Sydney, and Kuala Lumpur have also been affected. At least 16 domestic flights to Bali were also cancelled, per local airport authorities.Anak Krakatoa is an active volcano that sits in the Sunda Strait, between the islands of Java and Sumatra.This is a developing story. https://www.dw.com/en/russia-arrests-swe.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OIJK Russia's FSB intelligence service released a video in which a Swedish man allegedly confessed to planning acts of terror in Russia on Ukraine's behalf Image: Russian State Media/REUTERS Advertisement Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) on Thursday announced the arrest and detention of a Swedish national that authorities say fights for Ukraine . What do we know so far? The 35-year-old Swede, detained near Pskov on Russia 's western border, has been charged with illegally entering the country and may face additional terrorism charges, said FSB representatives. Russia claims to have secured documents proving that the man led a Ukrainian drone unit. They are now investigating whether he could be charged with organizing terror attacks on behalf of Ukraine or other Western intelligence services. According to the FSB, the man "entered the Russian Federation under the pretext of joining the ranks of the Russian armed forces with the aim of carrying out acts of sabotage and terrorist attacks on military installations." The FSB also released a video that it claimed showed the man confessing that he had entered Russia to commit "terrorist attacks" and sabotage. Putin on a war footing: escalation on all fronts? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video During the video the man spoke in English, saying that he was from Stockholm, had signed a contract with Ukraine's Defense Ministry and had received drone training. Russian state TV showed images of what it said was the man's contract with Ukraine. The Pskov region borders Belarus , Estonia and Latvia — the latter two being EU and NATO member states — FSB officials did not specify where exactly the man had arrived from. Sweden aware of incident, with no comment yet from Ukraine The Swedish Foreign Ministry has said that it is aware of the situation but not involved. Ukraine has not commented on the arrest. On Tuesday, Russia arrested a Japanese journalist that Moscow accused of spying, a claim that Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi rejected. Russia itself has been accused of hiring and deploying numerous individuals to commit acts of sabotage abroad or to recruit locals willing to do so — this, beyond the country's legions of malign cyber actors . None of the claims made by Russia and the FSB on Thursday can be substantiated.
